claims.claim: The study reports that participants sometimes simplified sentence structure or removed flowery language, giving the example of cutting a phrase about a spirit whose generosity knew no bounds down to an amazing man.
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: participants sometimes simplified sentence structure or removed flowery language

claims.claim: The same study observed that other participants added cliched expressions during post-editing, which the authors take as evidence that such language was not uniformly viewed as uncharacteristic.
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026

claims.claim: The study found a gap between perceived stylistic authenticity and model-measured similarity: post-edited text was often perceived by its own editor as representative of their personal style despite remaining detectable LLM stylistic traces.
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: despite remaining detectable LLM stylistic traces

claims.claim: The study's exploratory results suggest that adoption of the post-editing workflow is limited less by the effort of adjusting style than by a perceived lack of interesting or original content in the LLM-generated drafts.
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: a perceived lack of interesting or original content in LLM-generated drafts
claims.page: Section 6.5, (Why) Do Participants Like to Post-Edit?

claims.claim: Liang and colleagues measured LLM-assisted writing across four institutional registers from January 2022 to September 2024, on a corpus of 687,241 consumer complaints, 537,413 corporate press releases, 304.3 million job postings and 15,919 United Nations press releases.
claims.source: Weixin Liang, Yaohui Zhang, Mihai Codreanu, Jiayu Wang et al., Stanford and UW, arXiv:2502.09747, February 2025

claims.claim: The study estimates that LLM-assisted content in United Nations press releases rose from 3.1% in Q1 2023 to 10.1% in Q3 2023 and reached 13.7% by Q3 2024.
claims.source: Liang, Zhang, Codreanu, Wang et al., arXiv:2502.09747, February 2025
claims.page: Section on LLM Adoption in United Nations Press Releases

claims.claim: The study estimates LLM-modified content in Newswire corporate press releases peaked at 24.3% in December 2023 and stabilised at 23.8% through September 2024.
claims.source: Liang, Zhang, Codreanu, Wang et al., arXiv:2502.09747, February 2025
claims.quote: peaking at 24.3% in December 2023 and stabilizing at 23.8%

claims.claim: The study reports the consumer-complaint estimate rising from a baseline algorithm false positive rate of 1.5% to 15.3% by August 2023, with only a modest increase to 17.7% through August 2024.
claims.source: Liang, Zhang, Codreanu, Wang et al., arXiv:2502.09747, February 2025
claims.quote: rose sharply from a baseline algorithm false positive rate of 1.5% to 15.3%

claims.claim: Liang and colleagues state explicitly that their study did not directly measure homogenization, and only point to prior academic research as a reason to expect similar effects in job postings.
claims.source: Liang, Zhang, Codreanu, Wang et al., arXiv:2502.09747, February 2025
claims.quote: our study did not directly measure homogenization

claims.claim: Chakrabarty and colleagues hired professional writers to edit LLM-generated paragraphs and found the writers agree on undesirable idiosyncrasies in LLM-generated text, which the authors formalised into a seven-category taxonomy.
claims.source: Tuhin Chakrabarty, Philippe Laban et al., Salesforce AI Research, arXiv:2409.14509, September 2024
claims.quote: these writers agree on undesirable idiosyncrasies in LLM-generated text

claims.feature: other: what a human editor sees first
claims.claim: The seven edit categories the study's professional writers converged on are Cliche, Unnecessary/Redundant Exposition, Purple Prose, Poor Sentence Structure, Lack of Specificity and Detail, Awkward Word Choice and Phrasing, and Tense Inconsistency.
claims.source: Tuhin Chakrabarty, Philippe Laban et al., Salesforce AI Research, arXiv:2409.14509, September 2024
claims.page: Table 3 and Section 4.4, Final Taxonomy for Fine-Grained Edits

claims.feature: other: what a human editor sees first
claims.claim: The LAMP corpus consists of 1,057 LLM-generated paragraphs edited by professional writers according to that taxonomy.

claims.quote: 1,057 LLM-generated paragraphs edited by professional writers

claims.claim: The models in that study were explicitly prompted to be original and were instructed not to use ornamental language and to focus on nuance, simplicity, and subtext, yet their output still drew the seven categories of expert edits.
